summary: Backend-only verification of session-19 mitigations on the admin bill-image path: Motor zstd/zlib compression, socketTimeoutMS 10s->20s, maxPoolSize=100/minPoolSize=10, and the one-shot 300ms retry inside GET /api/bills/{id}/image. Wrote 2 new suites (17 tests) plus re-ran the iteration 54-57 regression suites. Result: 95 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed. Retry behaviour proven with mock.patch.object(server, 'db', ...): first find_one raising pymongo NetworkTimeout then succeeding returns HTTP 200 with the REAL image_url (exactly 2 find_one calls, ~300ms backoff observed); both-fail returns 200 with fetch_error='Server error while loading image: ...'; a legitimate not-found is NOT retried (1 call) and returns 404 detail='Bill not found'. Latency probe on a seeded 4.20MB inline-base64 bill: raw motor find_one 5-6ms, end-to-end /image 117-393ms (cold-first 393ms) — three orders of magnitude inside the 20s socket budget on preview.

minor.issue: Stale comment says 'Snappy on the wire cuts that 3-5x' while the code now negotiates compressors='zstd,zlib'. Cosmetic only, but misleading for the next session.

The retry loop catches bare `except Exception`, so non-transient failures (bad projection, auth error, decode error) are also retried once, adding a needless 300ms. Narrowing to pymongo.errors.NetworkTimeout/AutoReconnect/ServerSelectionTimeoutError would be tighter, but current behaviour is safe (max 2 attempts, 404 path unaffected).

action_items: Optional: fix the stale 'Snappy' comment near the AsyncIOMotorClient init (code uses zstd,zlib).
Optional: narrow the /image retry except clause to pymongo NetworkTimeout/AutoReconnect.

Product-level (real root cause, still open): bills store multi-MB base64 image_url inline in the doc. Compression + 20s timeout is a mitigation, not a fix. Recommend moving image payloads to object storage (S3/GridFS) and keeping only a key in the bill doc — that removes the multi-MB Atlas read from the admin review hot path entirely and would also cut Atlas egress. Based on preview numbers (4.2MB doc read in ~6ms locally, endpoint ~120ms warm), Atlas tier scaling is NOT indicated by CPU/latency of the query itself; the exposure is network transfer of the fat doc, which zstd already reduces 3-5x.
critical_code_review_comments: pymongo 4.5.0 + zstandard 0.25.0 negotiate zstd correctly — verified via client.options.pool_options._compression_settings.compressors == ['zstd','zlib'] and a live read; no startup error in backend logs.
zstandard==0.25.0 is pinned in /app/backend/requirements.txt (verified by regex on the file).
get_bill_image's outer try/except still guarantees never-raw-500: both simulated retry exhaustion and generic errors return 200 + fetch_error.
404 path is evaluated after the retry loop on a successful (None) read, so not-found is not amplified into retries — confirmed by call counting.
server.py is ~9000 lines; still far past the 700-line guideline. Splitting into routers (bills, admin, whatsapp, loyalty) remains the biggest maintainability debt.

success_rate.backend: 100% (95 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed across iteration 54-58 suites)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Session-19 mitigations verified in preview. Retry proof technique: patch server.db with a fake object whose bills.find_one raises pymongo NetworkTimeout N times, then call `await server.get_bill_image(bill_id, payload={'role':'admin'})` directly on a single shared event loop (motor binds to the first loop). Two stale assertions in iteration_56/57 suites were updated (socket timeout 20s; unset reprocessing_started_at before re-triggering reprocess) — reuse those files as-is. Preview MONGO_URL is local mongodb, so preview latency numbers do NOT prove Atlas behaviour; the production Haldiram's bill is still not reproducible here. If the production timeout recurs, the remaining fix is to stop storing multi-MB base64 inline in bills docs.
rca_of_the_issue: Production timeout root cause is unchanged: bills docs embed multi-MB base64 image_url, so a single find_one must pull megabytes over the Atlas wire; when Atlas/network is slow this exceeded socketTimeoutMS and the handler's outer except turned it into the 'Server error while loading image' fetch_error the admin saw. Session-19 reduces the probability (zstd wire compression 3-5x smaller payload, 20s instead of 10s budget, warm pool of 10 connections, one 300ms retry for transient blips) but does not remove the fat-document read. Preview measurements: 4.2MB doc find_one 5-6ms, /image endpoint 117-393ms — i.e. well under budget locally; the Atlas gap is network transfer, so object storage for images (or a projection that streams the image separately) is the durable fix rather than scaling the Atlas tier.
